chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who makes an oath of abstention from his wife until four months pass. He said: He is suspended. If he decides on divorce, his wife observes the waiting period just as the divorced woman does. If he returns (to conjugal life), he keeps her, and there is no harm.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ: Four months, the specific duration mentioned for Ila
key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband who takes an oath of abstention (Ila) from his wife for four months?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the four-month period of 'Ila' serves as a probationary window; if the husband persists in abstaining, the wife is treated as divorced and observes the corresponding waiting period (Iddah). However, if he revokes his oath and resumes marital relations within this timeframe, the marriage remains intact without penalty, highlighting the juristic emphasis on reconciliation and the specific legal status of the wife during this interim period.
